scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
product_from_film: Content Rewards presents a way to fund creator-posted content campaigns and track their reach.
explains_well: The film turns a marketing claim into a visible comparison with spend, counting tools, campaign setup and result totals.
unclear: It treats counted passers-by and content views as comparable reach, without explaining attention, unique people, audience quality or business outcomes.
scenario: Compare a billboard campaign with a funded creator-content campaign.
product_clear_basis: A campaign form shows a $5,000 budget and Fund & Activate.

scenes.action: Monochrome Toronto streets and transit lead to a claim of spending $5,000 on a prominent billboard. Phone, typing, invoice and confirmation-message close-ups show preparation.
scenes.design: Black-and-white city footage shifts to warm orange device shots.
scenes.purpose: Set up a real-world spend experiment.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 0–10s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Text says cameras recorded people walking by and AI counted them. Billboard footage alternates with a terminal-like tracking view, orange person boxes and charts.
scenes.design: Documentary street views and dark technical monitoring screens.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 10–27s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Day-to-night billboard views carry increasing people counts and times. A card states 24,311 people saw the billboard, followed by 62 scanned the QR code.
scenes.design: Large white metrics over location footage, then black result cards.
scenes.purpose: Report the billboard side of the comparison.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 27–42s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A search for Content Rewards leads to a result and campaign form. The name is typed, budget is $5,000 and Fund & Activate appears.
scenes.design: Close crops of search and form fields.
scenes.purpose: Set up the alternative with a stated equal budget.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 42–50s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Video-submission cards show growing view totals. A map fills with points, social engagement figures appear and text counts to about 64 million logo views in 24 hours, then 11k link clicks. A content collage follows.
scenes.design: Dark dashboard, map and large numeric cards.
scenes.purpose: Show distributed content reach and response.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 50–64s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: A white sample leads to 2,500 times better wording. A tiny billboard circle is compared with a huge orange Content Rewards circle labeled 64,562,883. We’ve made our point leads to the Content Rewards mark and black ending.
scenes.design: Strong size contrast and minimal conclusion cards.
scenes.purpose: Make the comparison memorable and close the argument.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 64–73.073s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

lessons.keep: Expose the comparison setup and measurement artifacts before showing the conclusion.
lessons.avoid: Avoid converting visibility counters into claims about unique people or equivalent attention.
lessons.open: Spend currency and full costs, counting accuracy, unique reach, attribution, comparable outcomes and all audio remain unverified.
try: Compare two Tin campaign approaches with the same defined goal, budget and attribution window.
Show a compact table separating views, unique viewers, clicks and qualified outcomes beside the result graphic.

comparison.story: Set up a real-world spend experiment. → Show the counting method. → Report the billboard side of the comparison. → Set up the alternative with a stated equal budget. → Show distributed content reach and response. → Make the comparison memorable and close the argument.
